subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but sturdy dwarf rifleman build, stocky proportions with chunky shoulders, hands, and boots, structured around a skeleton with hips, spine, chest, head, and limbs, keeping the hand geometry simple while following the required role chain.

Working out the leg and spine joint coordinates using mirrored hip/knee/ankle points and a short spine chain up to the chest, then placing the neck and head joints with their aim directions.

For the torso I'm deciding between sweeping an ellipse profile along the spine path versus building it as simpler rigid part shapes attached to the spine chain joints, leaning toward the simpler rigid approach for reliability.

For the arms I'm laying out a relaxed A-pose, positioning shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints slightly extended outward and down, and naming the arm chains for the skeletal hierarchy.

For hands, I'm sketching simple fist shapes with separate finger capsules attached to the wrist bone via a loop rather than full digit chains. For the blunderbuss, I'm deciding to have the figure carry it in one hand, angled forward diagonally rather than held symmetrically in a T-pose, positioning the stock accordingly.

Writing weapon geometry...

Now I'm designing the head: a skull-shaped sphere with skin tones, a prominent nose, brow ridge, small dark eyes with a glint, and ears, topped with a riveted steel dwarf helmet with brass rim that leaves the face visible. I'm also starting on a large braided beard.

Adding beard geometry...

Adding a brass belt buckle, then moving to the legs with tapered sweep chains, boot geometry positioned at the ankle bone, and shoulder pauldrons made from scaled spheres...

For decoration, I'm planning two or three textures: an eye motif, a dwarf crest emblem for the chest, maybe a beard braid pattern — applying them as planes on the skull and tabard rather than risking decals, since a flat plane with texture is simpler and safer.

Working out eye placement using spherical coordinates on the skull surface, with azimuth around ±22 degrees and slight elevation, plus nose and head proportions to keep the face readable at small scale.

Now I'm adding facial features: a nose sphere tinted pinker, a brow ridge made from a rod shape, bushy eyebrow rods, and small pointed ears. I'm also sketching out a helmet as a lathe shape with a brim profile, checking that its base and brim height clear the skull and brow without clipping.

I'm thinking about adding helmet embellishments like a crest ridge and small horns for a Warcraft dwarf style, plus settling on a color palette: tan skin, red-orange beard, Ironforge blue tabard with gold trim, and brown leather accents.

Now I'm pulling in steel and brass paints from the clockwork kit for the armor and gun details, deciding glow effects are unnecessary here. I'm planning the braided beard as two side braids built along curved paths from the chin, with bead spheres threaded along each braid for a decorative finish.

Since the beard path points are plain literals without bone references, I'll let the system fall back to the nearest joint rather than forcing a bone assignment. For the main beard mass, I'm positioning and scaling a sphere to sit low on the chest beneath the chin.

Checking the overlap math, the beard's upper extent at y~1.29 would actually intrude into the eye region around y~1.255, which is a problem since the beard shouldn't cover the eyes. I'm recalculating with the beard centered lower, around y 1.07 with a smaller scale, so its top edge sits safely below the eyeline.

I'm sketching the jaw as a small hidden flesh sphere under the beard, separate from the skull, with mustache capsules swept outward and colored orange, and planning the neck and shoulders to tuck under the beard coverage.

Now I'm working out the torso: setting head height so the neck stays short above the chest, then building a spine chain with named joints (spine1, spine2, chest) so arms and neck can parent off the chest tip, and defining a sweep radius function that widens toward the shoulders with a slight oscillation for shape.

For coloring, I'm giving the torso a blue tabard look, considering painting the front panel differently from the sides, and adding a small decal plane on the chest front to act as a crest emblem, positioned just outside the torso surface with alpha cutoff so it reads as a flat badge rather than floating.

Now I'm roughing out the legs with tapered cylindrical sweeps in a dark brown pant color plus boot cylinders, and thinking through hand construction — simplifying away from individual finger capsules toward a chunky leather glove box shape with maybe a thumb capsule, since the gun grip just needs to pass through the hand geometry.

I'm also working out the pose: keeping both arms relaxed at the sides in a neutral stance, with the gun held in the right hand angled forward-upward, and computing the grip, butt, and barrel positions algebraically along a normalized direction vector from the wrist point.

Still building the gun model...

Now I'm adding accessories: a powder horn swept along a curve with a brass cap, belt pouches as boxes, and a leather backpack with a bedroll attached.

I'm working out the bandolier placement diagonally across the chest with brass shell cylinders, but noticing it conflicts spatially with the crest decal near the collar, so I need to reposition one of them to avoid overlap.

Actually, I'll move the crest off the chest entirely and instead place it on a hanging tabard cloth below the belt, adding a textured plane to its front face and positioning it just outside the thigh geometry so it clears the legs.

Adding pauldron spikes with cones pointing outward-up, then defining the eye decals as almond shapes with blue irises, and setting up beard grain texture constants.

Now I'm working out the leg chain geometry: hip to knee to ankle positions, naming joints with side-based prefixes like hipL, and sizing the pants sweep radius. I'm placing the boot shaft cylinder to overlap the knee joint and sketching out the foot box dimensions.

Adding more foot details...

Now I'm setting up the skull and head joints on a neck-to-head bone chain, defining positions for neck and head with parent relationships back to the chest.

Continuing with the jaw joint and skull surface placement, then a jaw sphere part and a mustache swept along a curved path near the mouth.

Now I'm designing the braids as a path of points running down from the head, with staggered bead spheres along it colored to match the beard, brass torus bands near the bottom, and a brass tassel spike at the tip; I'm also adding a second lower beard mass sphere and offsetting the braid spheres in a zigzag for a woven look.

Moving to the helmet: I'm building it with a lathed brass rim ring, skipping a nose guard, and adding bone-colored horn cones jutting outward from the sides, plus extruding a crest profile along the helmet's length for a decorative ridge.

Then for the body, I'm adding glove boxes and thumb capsules at the wrists, with the right hand set to grip the gun. The backpack gets a box shape with a horizontal bedroll cylinder, a pot sphere, and two shoulder strap rods.

Now I'm working out the flintlock's lock mechanism, orienting a small box along the barrel direction, adding a hammer rod and brass pan sphere, skipping the trigger guard torus in favor of a simple rod, and planning a powder horn as a catmull curve sweep—keeping the total line count manageable while watching for TypeScript type issues.

I'm setting up helper functions for rods and offset points along the direction vector, adding a glowing ember sphere for the pan, and sketching out eye textures with almond shapes and iris coloring plus a blue-and-gold shield crest design.

For the crest, I'm crossing a hammer and rifle with simple geometric shapes, sizing the viewBox accordingly, and positioning the tabard plane geometry on the front face. Now I'm ready to write out the final export code.
